meta.title: TexLite · A lightweight collaborative LaTeX workspace

hero.eyebrow: A lightweight workspace for research writing
hero.title: Make LaTeX feel effortless.
hero.lead: TexLite brings editing, compilation, preview, and collaboration into a calm browser workspace while keeping the LaTeX environment you already trust.

highlights.title: One workspace from source to paper
highlights.lead: A concise view of TexLite's trade-offs: keep the LaTeX environment you know while bringing writing, compilation, and collaboration into one private space.
highlights.note: One practical distinction: Overleaf's hosted service can queue, slow down, or time out during usage peaks; Overleaf's open-source Docker deployment requires a more involved service stack and does not include key collaboration features such as comments.

items.title: Core capabilities
items.body: Edit, compile, preview, and collaborate in the browser with outline navigation, comments, SyncTeX, and structured diagnostics.

items.title: Why choose TexLite
items.body: Keep data on your server without sharing compilation resources with a public instance; keep the service small for teams that already have LaTeX.

items.title: From source to paper
items.body: Use the host's LaTeX directly, open the latest PDF when you return, and move between PDF, source, and comments as you work.

deploy.title: A few commands to own your writing space.
deploy.lead: TexLite does not expose public registration. Create the administrator during initialization, then let the administrator add the team.

docker.title: Start without maintaining host dependencies.
docker.lead: Do not want to maintain Node.js, TeX Live, Git, and Harper on the host? Use the released TexLite-Docker image while keeping configuration and project data mounted on your server.

closing.title: Let's build something great.
closing.lead: TexLite is open source, self-hosted, and made for the way research teams actually write.

footer.tagline: A lightweight, private, collaborative LaTeX workspace
